label: SYNTHETIC PORTFOLIO EXERCISE
allocation: Complete randomization, fixed equal allocation, shuffled account IDs before onboarding
primary: Any completed workout in elapsed days 22-28 after assignment, inclusive
diagnostic: First completed workout by elapsed day 7, inclusive
paid_guardrail: Any first paid conversion by elapsed day 28
error_guardrail: Any logged onboarding error in elapsed days 0-7
ci_method: Newcombe difference of independent Wilson score intervals, uncorrected
decision_order: If retention upper CI < 0, retain current timing due to retention harm
If paid upper CI < -1.0pp or error lower CI > 0.5pp, retain current timing due to guardrail harm
If retention point estimate >= 1.5pp AND lower CI > 0 AND paid lower CI > -1.0pp AND error upper CI < 0.5pp, recommend simulated rollout
Otherwise retain current timing pending more evidence or a revised design
scope: Hypothetical consumer fitness app. Same optional weekly goal prompt, wording and skip option. Control sees prompt on onboarding day 0; treatment sees it just after the first completed workout. Assignment is permanent. Goal capture is disconnected from workout selection and other features in both arms.
assumptions: 40,000 distinct eligible new accounts have completed 28 days of follow-up; no bot, employee or repeat-account exclusions are made after assignment.
All account assignment and outcome logging is complete. Accounts without a workout remain in the denominator with retention=0.
No interference across accounts; repeated devices resolve to the same account. All assigned accounts open onboarding and the control prompt is rendered.
Among accounts without an early first workout, 8% first complete one on days 8-21; otherwise there is no workout by day 28. This simplification omits first-ever workouts on days 22-28.

Workout outcomes are linked through early/late first-workout status. Payment and error outcomes are independent Bernoulli draws, a deliberate simplification rather than an empirical behavioural model.
Prompt seen is an exposure event, not evidence of accepting a goal. A late-retention difference does not establish a commitment mechanism.
Effect sizes, rates, sample size and thresholds are analyst-chosen educational assumptions and have no calibration to any real app, company or client data.
One fixed-horizon analysis after all follow-up. Diagnostic and sensitivity outcomes are descriptive. The rollout rule is a conjunction of prespecified requirements, with no fishing among metrics.
The same frozen random draws are reused across sensitivity scenarios for comparison; scenarios are alternative data-generating assumptions, not independent experiments. No seed search or rerolling.
Intervals quantify random sampling variation inside the synthetic model; they do not quantify uncertainty about real users.
